references.text: The same principle of cursing parents with the death penalty as a consequence is found here in Exodus, which is the original legislation that Leviticus 20:9 builds upon.
A curse is pronounced over anyone who dishonors their father or mother, emphasizing the seriousness of respecting one's parents.
Proverbs warns that whoever curses their father or mother will have their lamp extinguished in darkness, a parallel to the death penalty in Leviticus.
Describes a generation that curses their father and does not bless their mother, showing that this was an ongoing problem in Israel.
Jesus quotes this commandment when he confronts the Pharisees about their tradition of korban, confirming the validity of the Mosaic law to honor parents.
Mark recounts Jesus' reference to this commandment in the context of criticizing the Pharisees for bypassing parental honor through traditions.
